10:2.headline: התרשתא is Nehemiah's title, from "they permitted him to drink"
10:2.body: Rashi says התרשתא is another name for Nehemiah, not a second man. He says the sages gave him that name because they permitted him to drink wine poured for idols, since he was the king's cupbearer.

sources.quote: שֵׁם אֶחָד הוּא, וְזֶהוּ שֶׁפֵּרַשְׁתִּי (עזרא ב:סג) דְּהַתִּרְשָׁתָא הוּא נְחֶמְיָה. וְלָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמוֹ הַתִּרְשָׁתָא? שֶׁהִתִּירוּ לוֹ חֲכָמִים לִשְׁתּוֹת יֵין נֶסֶךְ, לְפִי שֶׁהָיָה מַשְׁקֶה לַמֶּלֶךְ
sources.says: Rashi says it is one name, and Tirshata is Nehemiah. It was called so because the sages permitted him to drink libation wine, since he served the king drink.

10:29.headline: "Everyone who knows and understands": able to teach, or able to grasp?
10:29.body: Ralbag reads it as people with the knowledge to hear and teach the words of the Torah. Metzudat David reads it more loosely: anyone who can understand something.

sources.quote: ר"ל אשר יהיו מהם בני דעת לשמוע וללמד את דברי התורה
sources.says: Ralbag says it means those among them with the knowledge to hear and to teach the words of the Torah.

sources.quote: כל יודע מבין. כל מי שיודע להבין בדבר מה
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means anyone who knows how to understand something.

10:34.headline: "The daily offering" here: incense, or a meal offering?
10:34.body: Ralbag says מנחת התמיד is the incense burned on the golden altar. Metzudat David says it is the meal offering that goes with the libations of the daily offerings.

sources.quote: ומנחת התמיד. הוא הקטורת שהיו מקטירים במזבח הזהב
sources.says: Ralbag says מנחת התמיד is the incense burned on the golden altar.

sources.quote: ומנחת התמיד. מנחת נסכי התמידין
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is the meal offering of the libations of the daily offerings.

10:35.headline: Wood is called an "offering" (קרבן)
10:35.body: Rashi says קרבן העצים means bringing the wood for the altar's fire near. In his comment on Menachot he says wood is called a קרבן because of this verse.

sources.quote: קֻרְבַּן הָעֵצִים. תִּקְרֹבֶת שֶׁל עֲצֵי הַמַּעֲרָכָה לַמִּזְבֵּחַ
sources.says: Rashi says קרבן העצים is the bringing near of the wood of the altar's arrangement.

sources.quote: עצים - נקראו קרבן שנאמר והגורלות הפלנו על קרבן העצים
sources.says: Rashi says wood is called an offering, as it says: we cast lots for the wood offering.

10:37.headline: "Our animals" here means the unclean ones, like the donkey
10:37.body: Ibn Ezra says בהמתנו here means unclean animals, because the verse goes on to name the firstborn of cattle and sheep. Malbim agrees. Metzudat David says it is the firstborn donkey, redeemed with a lamb.

sources.quote: רצה לומר בהמתנו בהמה טמאה, כי אחרי כן בכורות בקרינו וצאננו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says בהמתנו means an unclean animal, since afterward it names the firstborn of our cattle and flock.

sources.quote: היינו בהמה טמאה, שא"צ להביא הפדיון לבית ה'
sources.says: Malbim says it means an unclean animal, whose redemption need not be brought to the Temple.

sources.quote: ובהמתנו. זה פטר חמור לפדותו בשה
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is the firstborn donkey, to be redeemed with a lamb.

12:25.headline: Gatherings, or the thresholds of the gates?
12:25.body: Rashi and Ibn Ezra read באספי as ספים, thresholds, with an extra alef, so the guards stood at the gate thresholds. Ralbag keeps the sense of gathering: Levites gathered at the gates.

sources.quote: כְּמוֹ בְּסִפֵּי הַשְּׁעָרִים
sources.says: Rashi says it means the same as בספי השערים, at the thresholds of the gates.

sources.quote: האל"ף נוסף והטעם שומרי הספים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the alef is extra and the meaning is guards of the thresholds.

sources.quote: שהם היו ראשים ללוים הנאספים אל השערים לשמרם
sources.says: Ralbag says they led the Levites who gathered at the gates to guard them.

12:31.headline: Two thanksgivings: loaves of bread, or two choirs?
12:31.body: Rashi says each תודה here is a loaf of thanksgiving bread carried around the city. Ibn Ezra says they were groups of singers, named for the song of thanks they sang.

sources.quote: שְׁתֵּי לַחְמֵי תוֹדָה, כָּל לֶחֶם וָלֶחֶם קָרוּי תּוֹדָה
sources.says: Rashi says these were two loaves of thanksgiving bread, and each loaf is called a תודה.

sources.quote: נקראו כן, כי הם מעמידין להודות לשם והם האומרים שיר של תודה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says they were called this because they stood to thank God and sang the song of thanks.

12:31.headline: Processions, or walkways built along the wall?
12:31.body: ותהלכת is a rare noun from הלך, to walk. Ibn Ezra reads it as people walking in procession, while Ralbag reads it as walkways built on the wall.

sources.quote: שם על משקל: תנחומות אל והוא מענין הלך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is a noun shaped like תנחומות and comes from the root meaning to walk.

sources.quote: ששם היו בנוים מקומות יוכלו להלוך בהם
sources.says: Ralbag says places were built there that people could walk along.

12:42.headline: "They made it heard," or one more name in the list?
12:42.body: Read plainly, וישמיעו says the singers made their voices heard. Metzudat David says it is a man's name, one more name in the list.

sources.quote: וישמיעו. כן שם איש
sources.says: Metzudat David says וישמיעו is the name of a man.

sources.quote: ואז וישמיעו המשוררים את קולם
sources.says: Malbim reads it as the singers raising their voices.

13:13.headline: A verb made from the word for storehouse
13:13.body: ואוצרה is a verb built from אוצרות, storehouses. Ibn Ezra and Metzudat David say it means Nehemiah put treasurers in charge of the stores.

sources.quote: פועל נגזר מן אוצרות והטעם: הפקדתי גזבר עליהם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is a verb taken from the word for storehouses, meaning 'I appointed a treasurer over them'.

sources.quote: שמתי אוצרים ר״ל ממונים וגזברים על האוצרות
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means he set officers and treasurers over the storehouses.

13:19.headline: The gates 'grew shadowed': the Friday evening shade reached them
13:19.body: צללו is a verb made from צל, shadow. Rashi and Ibn Ezra say it marks the time when the late-afternoon shadows fell on the city gates before the Sabbath.

sources.quote: כַּאֲשֶׁר נָטוּ הַצְּלָלִים שֶׁל עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת בַּשְּׁעָרִים
sources.says: Rashi says it means when the shadows of Sabbath eve stretched over the gates.

sources.quote: מענין צל והטעם הגעת הצל אל השערים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it comes from shadow, meaning the shade reached the gates.

sources.quote: כאשר האריכו צללי השערים והוא לפנות הערב
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is when the gates' shadows grew long, toward evening.

13:20.headline: Spice sellers, or traders in everything, which is why gossips are רכיל
13:20.body: Metzudat Zion says רוכלים are perfume sellers. Ralbag says they are simply merchants. Ibn Ezra says they mix many kinds of goods, and that is why a person who mixes up stories is called a רכיל, a gossip.

sources.quote: הרוכלים. מוכרי הבושם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the רוכלים are sellers of perfume.

sources.quote: וילינו הרוכלים. הם הסוחרים
sources.says: Ralbag says the רוכלים are the merchants.

sources.quote: הסוחרים מערבים ענינים רבים, על כן מערב הדברים נקרא רכיל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says these traders mix many goods, so one who mixes up words is called רכיל.

13:23.headline: They 'seated' foreign women: a way of saying they married them
13:23.body: The verb השיבו, from 'sit', is used here for taking wives. Rashi and Metzudat David say they settled these women in their homes as wives.

sources.quote: אֲשֶׁר נָשְׂאוּ לָהֶם נָשִׁים שֶׁל עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים
sources.says: Rashi says it means they married women from the idol-worshipping nations.

sources.quote: הושיבו בבתיהם לקחתם לנשים
sources.says: Metzudat David says they settled them in their homes, taking them as wives.

13:25.headline: 'I cursed them' means he put them under a ban
13:25.body: ואקללם usually means 'I cursed them'. Ibn Ezra and Ralbag say it was a formal ban: Nehemiah excommunicated them.

sources.quote: הוא החרם והנדוי והטעם החרמתים נדיתים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the curse was the ban and excommunication.

sources.quote: הנה קצתם נדה והחרים
sources.says: Ralbag says he banned and excommunicated some of them.

13:25.headline: He pulled out their hair, a punishment beyond what the Torah sets
13:25.body: ואמרטם means he tore out their hair. Ralbag says the Torah sets no such penalty. Nehemiah did it as a one-time measure because the generation had broken down on this.

sources.quote: ענין תלישת השער כמו ואיש כי ימרט ראשו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means pulling out hair, as in Leviticus 13:40.

sources.quote: ואם אין הקללה והמריטה ראויה לפי מה שהטילה התורה מהעונשים על זה. אך עשה זה נחמיה להוראת שעה
sources.says: Ralbag says the cursing and hair-pulling are not Torah penalties, but Nehemiah used them as a one-time ruling.

13:27.headline: 'Is it heard?' here means 'Shall we obey you?'
13:27.body: שמע can mean to hear or to accept and obey. Maimonides lists this verse where it means to accept. Ibn Ezra reads הנשמע as 'shall we listen to you' and do this great evil.

sources.quote: וכמוהו לרוב גם "שמע" במשמעות של קבלה
sources.says: Maimonides says שמע often means accepting, and cites this verse.

sources.quote: יתכן שהוא נפעל מן העתיד, סימן המדברים בעד עצמם והוא הקרוב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it may be a first-person plural future, 'shall we', and he thinks that is the closer reading.

13:29.headline: Not the 'redeeming' גאל but the one that means to defile
13:29.body: גאל often means to redeem. Here the commentators read it as filth and disgust. The priests who married foreign wives soiled the priesthood.

sources.quote: ענין טנוף ומאוס כמו ויגאלו מן הכהונה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means filth and disgust, like 'they were defiled from the priesthood'.

sources.quote: שהיו מטנפים דבר הכהונה בהתערבם בגויי הארץ
sources.says: Ralbag says they were soiling the priesthood by mixing with the local nations.

2:1.headline: Artaxerxes: a royal title, like Pharaoh
2:1.body: Rashi and the Metzudat Zion say this king is Darius. They say ארתחשסתא is the title of the Persian throne, the way every king of Egypt is called Pharaoh.

sources.quote: וְעַל שֵׁם הַמַּלְכוּת נִקְרָא כָּךְ
sources.says: Rashi says the king is Darius and is called by this name after the kingdom.

sources.quote: הוא דריוש הפרסי ונקרא כן ע״ש המלכות כמו פרעה למצרים
sources.says: The Metzudat Zion says it is Darius the Persian, called this after the kingdom, as Pharaoh is the name for Egypt's kings.

2:2.headline: A sad heart, or a heart plotting to poison the king?
2:2.body: Ralbag thinks the king meant it kindly, 'you must be troubled', though it could be heard as anger. Rashi and the Metzudat David hear suspicion: the king fears his cupbearer has poisoned the cup, which is why Nehemiah was so afraid.

sources.quote: ידמה שאמר לו זה על צד אהבה
sources.says: Ralbag thinks the king said this out of affection.

sources.quote: ולפי שזה המאמר היה אפשר שיובן שנאמר על דרך השנאה והכעס היה ירא נחמיה
sources.says: Ralbag says the words could be taken as hatred and anger, so Nehemiah was afraid.

sources.quote: שֶׁיֵּשׁ בִּלְבָבְךָ עָלַי לַהֲמִיתֵנִי בְּסַם הַמָּוֶת בִּשְׁתִיַּת כּוֹס זֶה
sources.says: Rashi says the king means: you have it in your heart to kill me with poison in this cup.

sources.quote: ר״ל לבך רע עלי להמיתני בשתיית זה הכוס אשר נתת בו דבר ארסי
sources.says: The Metzudat David says the king means: your heart is set on killing me with poison you put in this cup.

2:3.headline: Why speak of graves? Persians held ancestors' graves holy
2:3.body: Nehemiah tells the king that Jerusalem, 'the city of my fathers' graves', lies in ruins. Malbim says this reason worked because the Persians held their ancestors' graves dear and holy.

sources.quote: כי מקום קברות האבות היה יקר וקדוש בעיני הפרסיים
sources.says: Malbim says the place of one's fathers' graves was precious and holy to the Persians.

sources.quote: אֲשֶׁר הָעִיר יְרוּשָׁלַיִם, שֶׁהִיא בֵּית קִבְרוֹת אֲבוֹתַי, חֲרֵבָה
sources.says: Rashi says the city meant is Jerusalem, where his fathers are buried.

2:4.headline: A prayer in the middle of talking with the king
2:4.body: Nehemiah prays between the king's question and his own answer. The Metzudat David says it was a short prayer said standing before the king, Ibn Ezra says he had prayed earlier, and Malbim says his words 'if it please the king' were meant in his heart for God.

sources.quote: עד שלא השיב אמריו התפלל לה׳ תפלה קצרה בעמדו לפני המלך
sources.says: The Metzudat David says before he answered, he prayed a short prayer to God while standing before the king.

sources.quote: ואתפלל אל אלהי השמים - וכבר התפללתי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means 'I had already prayed'.

sources.quote: שמ"ש אם על המלך טוב היה בלבו אל המלך העליון
sources.says: Malbim says that when he said 'if it please the king', in his heart he meant the King above.

2:8.headline: A פרדס that supplies beams: orchard, or the king's forest?
2:8.body: פרדס usually means an orchard of fruit trees, as the Metzudat Zion says. Here it supplies timber for gates and walls, and Rashi and Malbim say its keeper was in charge of the king's forests.

sources.quote: הפרדס. הוא גן מעץ פרי
sources.says: The Metzudat Zion says a פרדס is a garden of fruit trees.

sources.quote: שׁוֹמֵר הַפַּרְדֵּס. מְמֻנֶּה הָיָה עַל הַיְּעָרִים אֲשֶׁר לַמֶּלֶךְ
sources.says: Rashi says the keeper was appointed over the king's forests.

sources.quote: שומר הפרדס, והוא היה ממונה על יערות הלבנון שהיו למלך
sources.says: Malbim says he was in charge of the king's forests of Lebanon.

2:8.headline: 'The house I will go to', not 'my house'
2:8.body: Nehemiah asks for wood for 'the house I will go to'. Malbim says the king built a house for the governor in every province and it stayed the king's, so Nehemiah did not call it his own.

sources.quote: כי המלך היה בונה בית בכל מדינה שישב בו הפחה והבית היה של המלך, לכן לא אמר לביתי
sources.says: Malbim says the king built a house in every province for the governor, and it belonged to the king, so he did not say 'my house'.

sources.quote: ולבית אשר אבוא אליו - הוא בית המלך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is the king's house.

2:13.headline: Was Nehemiah breaking the wall, or examining it?
2:13.body: Rashi and the Metzudat David read שבר as 'breaking': Nehemiah secretly made more holes in the wall, so the people would think enemies did it and rush to rebuild. Ibn Ezra reads the letter ש with the other dot, from 'to examine': he was studying the walls.

sources.quote: וְהָיִיתִי פּוֹרֵץ בַּחוֹמָה, וְהַחוֹמָה הָיְתָה נוֹחָה לְהַפִּילָהּ
sources.says: Rashi says Nehemiah was breaking into the wall, which was easy to knock down.

sources.quote: וְהֵם הָלְכוּ לִשְׁבֹּר וּלְהַפִּיל חוֹמוֹת הָעִיר בַּלַּיְלָה, וּלְהַרְבּוֹת פִּרְצוֹתֶיהָ
sources.says: Rashi says they went at night to break down the walls and add more breaches, so the city's people would be eager to rebuild.

sources.quote: כונתו היתה למען יחשבו אנשי ירושלים שהאויב הוא השובר את החומה ויעוררו לבם לבנותה ולחזקה
sources.says: The Metzudat David says he meant the people to think the enemy broke the wall, and so be stirred to rebuild it.

sources.quote: והטעם הייתי חושב ומעיין בחומות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means 'I was thinking about and examining the walls'.

sources.quote: ונוסחת הראב"ע היא בשי"ן שמאלית ופי' מענין סברה שעיין בחומה
sources.says: Malbim notes that Ibn Ezra's text has the letter sin, read as 'examining' the wall.

sources.quote: ואהי חושב בחומות ירושלים אשר הם פרוצים
sources.says: Ralbag reads it as 'I was considering the broken walls of Jerusalem'.

2:13.headline: Two words written as one, and an open letter for open walls
2:13.body: The written text joins two words as המפרוצים, and the reading tradition splits them into הם פרוצים, 'which were broken'. Ibn Ezra reports a homily that the open letter מ inside the word hints at the open, breached walls, but he prefers the plain reading.

sources.quote: רק אנשי המסורת הפרידום לקצר המלות ולפרש המ"ם הפתוחה רמז לחומות הפתוחות ופרוצות, הוא דרך דרש והדרך הראשון בעיני נכון
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the Masoretes split the words, and calls the idea that the open מ hints at open, breached walls a homily; he prefers the first, plain way.

sources.quote: אֲשֶׁר הֵם פְּרוּצִים. שֶׁהֵם אוֹתָם מְקוֹמוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ פְּרוּצִים
sources.says: Rashi reads it as 'which were breached': the places already broken through.

2:16.headline: Nobles are 'the white ones', the lowly 'the dark ones'
2:16.body: חרים is a word for nobles. The Metzudat Zion says it comes from חיור, white, the opposite of lowly people, who are called חשוכים, dark, in Proverbs.

sources.quote: ולחורים. כן יקראו השרים הגדולים והוא מל׳ חיור ולובן הפוך מן השפלים הנקראים חשוכים
sources.says: The Metzudat Zion says great officials are called חורים, from whiteness, the opposite of the lowly, who are called 'dark ones'.

2:20.headline: 'No share, no צדקה': not even a donation
2:20.body: Ralbag and Ibn Ezra read צדקה as charity: the enemies may not even give money to the building, which would earn them credit in Jerusalem. Malbim reads it as merit: they have none, since they do not serve God.

sources.quote: גם לא יתנו מהונם לעזור בזה מה שיחשב להם צדקם
sources.says: Ralbag says they will not give of their money to help, which would count as charity for them.

sources.quote: אינכם ראויים שתעשו צדקה בבנין ביתו, שתהיו נזכרים לפניו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says they are not fit to give charity for building God's house and be remembered before him.

sources.quote: ולא צדקה, כי אינכם עובדים את ה'
sources.says: Malbim says they have no צדקה because they do not serve God.

3:1.headline: The priests 'sanctified' the gate, or simply got it ready
3:1.body: קדשוהו usually means they made it holy. Rashi and Metzudat David say the priests gave the gate the holiness of the city. Ralbag reads it as 'they prepared it', by building the wall on both sides.

sources.quote: לְאוֹתוֹ שַׁעַר בִּקְדֻשַּׁת הָעִיר
sources.says: Rashi says they gave that gate the holiness of the city.

sources.quote: קדשו אותו בפה להיות קדוש בקדושת העיר
sources.says: Metzudat David says they declared it holy aloud, with the holiness of the city.

sources.quote: ואמר שהמה קדשוהו ר"ל שהכינוהו כי בנו החומה מימינו ומשמאלו
sources.says: Ralbag says it means they prepared it, building the wall on its right and left.

3:5.headline: The nobles refused the work of their 'lords': God, or their overseers?
3:5.body: The nobles of Tekoa would not bend their necks to 'the work of their lords'. Rashi and Metzudat David say the lord is God, since building the wall was a holy task. Ibn Ezra and Malbim say it means the human officers over them.

sources.quote: לֹא סִיְּעוּ בַּעֲבוֹדָתוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says they did not help in the work of the Holy One, building the city wall.

sources.quote: שהוא עבודת האדון ה׳ כי הבנין הזה למצוה יחשב
sources.says: Metzudat David says it was the work of the Lord, since this building counts as a commandment.

sources.quote: האדון והשר הממונה עליהם ממשפחתם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the lord is the officer from their own family who was placed over them.

sources.quote: רק שהם לא הביאו צוארם בעבודת אדוניהם מפני שהיו אדירים והיו חפשים לעצמם
sources.says: Malbim says they did not submit to their masters because they were powerful and free men.

3:8.headline: They did not 'abandon' Jerusalem, they packed it with earth
3:8.body: ויעזבו usually means 'they abandoned'. Here the commentators read it from the sages' word מעזיבה, a packed layer of earth: they filled in the wall to make it strong.

sources.quote: מִלְּאוּהָ עָפָר עַד הַחוֹמָה הָרְחָבָה, כְּדֵי לְהַחֲזִיקָהּ
sources.says: Rashi says they filled it with earth up to the broad wall to strengthen it.

sources.quote: ענינו מלוי העפר לחזוק ובדרז״ל תקרה ומעזיבה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means filling in earth for strength, like the sages' phrase 'a ceiling and its packed layer'.

sources.quote: מלשון חכמים מעזיבה. ויש אומרים: כי כן: עזוב תעזוב עמו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra takes it from the sages' word מעזיבה, and notes others link it to 'you shall surely help him'.

3:12.headline: Shallum built with his daughters, or with his district's villages
3:12.body: Rashi reads 'he and his daughters' plainly: Shallum's daughters helped build the wall. Ralbag offers another reading: the 'daughters' are the small towns of his district, as big cities had daughter towns.

sources.quote: שַׁלּוּם וּבְנוֹתָיו הֶחֱזִיקוּ לִבְנוֹת הַבִּנְיָן
sources.says: Rashi says Shallum and his daughters joined in the building.

sources.quote: ידמה שבנות שלום עזרוהו בבנין או שב כנוי בנותיו אל הפלך והנה היו לירושלים בנות כמנהג העירות הגדולות
sources.says: Ralbag says either Shallum's daughters helped him, or 'daughters' refers to the district, since Jerusalem had daughter towns like other big cities.

3:12.headline: Son of 'the whisperer': a title or a name?
3:12.body: הלוחש means 'the whisperer'. Ibn Ezra says the word 'the' suggests a title, not a personal name. Malbim says the ה is part of the name itself.

sources.quote: יתכן להיות שם תואר בעבור ה"א הדעת, כי לא יכנס על שם עצם אדם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it may be a title, because 'the' is not put before a person's own name.

sources.quote: הלוחש הה"א מעיקר השם
sources.says: Malbim says the ה is part of the name.

3:15.headline: He 'shaded' the gate: roofed it, from the word for shade
3:15.body: ויטללנו appears only here. Rashi, Ibn Ezra and Metzudat Zion read it from the Aramaic word for shade, טלל, so he roofed the gate over.

sources.quote: וְהוּא הָיָה מְסַכֵּךְ אוֹתוֹ, לְשׁוֹן מְטַלַלְתָּא
sources.says: Rashi says he covered it over, from the Aramaic word for a covering.

sources.quote: הוא ענין צל כי בצל קורתי (בראשית י״ט:ח׳) ת״א בטלל
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means shade, since the Targum renders 'in the shadow of my roof' with בטלל.

sources.quote: מתרגום בצל קורתי בטלל שירותי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it comes from the Targum's word for 'in the shadow of my roof'.

3:20.headline: Baruch 'burned' to build: with zeal, with anger, or a name?
3:20.body: החרה comes from a root meaning heat or anger. Metzudat David reads it as zeal: Baruch warmed to the work. Ibn Ezra says he was angry at himself over the delay. Malbim reads החרה as a man's name.

sources.quote: התחמם בזריזות רב והחזיק שוב
sources.says: Metzudat David says he warmed himself with great zeal and built again.

sources.quote: מלשון חרון והטעם החרה אפו על עצמו על עכוב המלאכה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is from the word for anger: he was angry at himself over the delay in the work.

sources.quote: החרה, שם איש
sources.says: Malbim says החרה is the name of a man.

sources.quote: פִּתְרוֹנוֹ לְפִי עִנְיָנוֹ, וְכֶפֶל לָשׁוֹן הוּא עַל הַחִזּוּק
sources.says: Rashi says it is explained by context, as a doubled word for building up.

3:33.headline: Sanballat burned inside first, then showed his anger
3:33.body: The verse uses two words for anger. Metzudat David and Malbim say ויחר is anger felt inside, and ויכעס is anger shown outside. Malbim adds the sages' reading that a face 'burns' like a scorched cake.

sources.quote: ויחר לו. בלב
sources.says: Metzudat David says ויחר means he was angry in his heart.

sources.quote: ואמרו חז"ל ויחר לדוד שנשתנו פניו כחררה), והכעס הוא אם יתגלה לחוץ
sources.says: Malbim cites the sages that David's face changed like a scorched cake, and says כעס is anger that shows outside.

3:34.headline: Sanballat's taunt: 'Will they be left alone?' or 'Will they fortify?'
3:34.body: Rashi reads היעזבו as 'will the nations leave them alone to build?'. Metzudat Zion and Malbim read it as in verse 8: 'will they pack the wall with earth and make it strong?'.

sources.quote: וְכִי הֵם סְבוּרִים אֲשֶׁר יַעַזְבוּ וְיַנִּיחוּ לָהֶם הָעוֹבְדֵי כוֹכָבִים לִבְנוֹת
sources.says: Rashi reads it as: do they think the nations will leave them alone to build?

sources.quote: מלשון מעזיבה והוא מלוי העפר לחזוק
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it comes from מעזיבה, filling in earth to strengthen.

sources.quote: היעזבו להם, מענין חיזוק. כמו ויעזבו את ירושלים
sources.says: Malbim says it means strengthening, as in 'they fortified Jerusalem' earlier in the chapter.

3:34.headline: Can they bring burnt stones back to life?
3:34.body: Sanballat mocks the builders: will they 'revive' the stones? Ibn Ezra explains that a burnt stone counts as dead. Ralbag says fire destroys the nature that made it a stone.

sources.quote: כי האבן השרופה כמת היא נחשבת
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says a burnt stone is counted as dead.

sources.quote: ולזה תדמה השרפה בהם למות כי הסירה מהם המהות אשר היו בו אבנים
sources.says: Ralbag says burning is like death for stones, since it takes away what made them stones.

sources.quote: תפסו על צד המליצה על האבנים שם מיתה וחיות
sources.says: Malbim says the speaker used death and life of stones as a figure of speech.

4:1.headline: The breached ones: holes in the wall, or exposed people?
4:1.body: הפרצים means the breached ones. Ralbag reads it as the gaps in the wall, while Rashi reads it as the people of the city, who had no wall around them until now.

sources.quote: אשר התחילו אנשי העיר שהיו פרוצים עד עתה מאין חומה
sources.says: Rashi says the breached ones are the city's people, who had been open to attack with no wall and were now closed in by it.

sources.quote: כי החלו המקומות הפרוצים להסתם
sources.says: Ralbag says it means the broken places in the wall began to close.

4:2.headline: The enemies planned תועה: damage, confusion, or a trick?
4:2.body: תועה comes from the root for going astray. Rashi reads it as wrecking the wall, Metzudat Zion as throwing the people into confusion, and Ralbag as fooling them so they would not see the attack coming.

sources.quote: לעשות לו בבנין החומה קלקול והשחתה
sources.says: Rashi says it means doing damage and ruin to the building of the wall.

sources.quote: המבולבל בדעתו לבלי דעת מה יעשה קרוי תועה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says a person so confused he does not know what to do is called תועה.

sources.quote: לעשות לעם ירושלים תועה שיתעו אותם שלא ידעו שהם רוצים להלחם בהם
sources.says: Ralbag says the plan was to mislead the people of Jerusalem so they would not know an attack was coming.

4:8.headline: The nobles are called "the white ones"
4:8.body: חרים means nobles, but the word is related to white. Ralbag says the Bible pictures the great in white for their joy, just as it pictures mourners in black.

sources.quote: השרים ומתאר אותם בלובן מצד שמחתם כמו שמתאר בעלי היגון בשחרות
sources.says: Ralbag says the word means the officials, described by whiteness for their joy, as people in grief are described by blackness.

4:16.headline: "Day" here runs from dawn until the stars come out
4:16.body: Verse 15 says they worked from dawn until the stars came out, and verse 16 calls that time the day. Ralbag learns from this that the whole span can be called day, even though the word first means the hours the sun is up.

sources.quote: ומזה המקום למדנו שכל זה הזמן אפשר שיקרא יום
sources.says: Ralbag says we learn from here that the whole time from dawn to the stars can be called day.

sources.quote: אלא שהיום יאמר בעצמות וראשונה על זמן עמידת השמש על הארץ
sources.says: Ralbag adds that the word day mainly and first means the time the sun stands over the earth.

6:3.headline: Sent "upon" them: a message they did not want
6:3.body: Nehemiah says he sent messengers עליהם, literally "upon them", not "to them". Malbim says "send" with על marks a message the other side does not want, and he cites this verse.

sources.quote: שלח הנקשר עם על מורה שנשלח לחברו בדבר שהוא שלא לרצונו
sources.says: Malbim says that "send" joined with על means sending someone a message against his wishes, and lists Nehemiah 6:3 as an example.

6:8.headline: בודאם: "you are making them up"
6:8.body: This verb, "to invent", is rare in the Bible. Ibn Ezra ties it to Jeroboam's feast "which he devised from his own heart", and to the later Hebrew word בדאי, "a liar".

sources.quote: מכזב, כמו: בדיך מתים יחרישו, בחדש אשר בדה מלבו. ובלשון חכמינו ז"ל: בדאי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means lying, as in "your lies silence men" and "the month which he devised from his heart", and the sages' word for a liar is בדאי.

sources.quote: ענין המצאת הכזב וכן בדיך מתים יחרישו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means inventing a lie, as in Job 11:3.

sources.quote: בְּלַעַ״ז, כְּמוֹ אֲשֶׁר בָּדָה מִלִּבּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi gives an Old French word for it and compares "which he devised from his heart".

6:9.headline: Who is afraid of whom?
6:9.body: מיראים looks like "they frighten us". Rashi turns it around: the nations are afraid of us, so they hope our hands will go slack. Metzudat David and Ibn Ezra read it as "you were frightening us".

sources.quote: מִתְיָרְאִים מִמֶּנּוּ, וְכָךְ הֵם אוֹמְרִים
sources.says: Rashi says they are afraid of us, and that is why they say "their hands will go slack".

sources.quote: שהרי לשעבר אתם כולכם הייתם מפחידים אותנו
sources.says: Metzudat David says Nehemiah tells Sanballat that in the past all of them were frightening us.

sources.quote: ופירש כלכם מפחדים אותנו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means all of you frighten us.

6:9.headline: Is "strengthen my hands" a request, or a statement?
6:9.body: חזק looks like a command. Ibn Ezra says Nehemiah says it to Sanballat, to calm him. Ralbag says it is not a command at all: now my hands grow stronger, because their lies failed.

sources.quote: לסנבלט הוא אומר על ידי פיוס
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says Nehemiah says this to Sanballat, to soothe him.

sources.quote: אין אמרו חזק צווי אלא הוא מקור
sources.says: Ralbag says חזק is not a command but a verbal noun: now my hand is strengthened by their failed lies.

6:10.headline: Why was Shemaiah "shut in"? Three answers
6:10.body: The verse only says Shemaiah was עצור, "held back". Ralbag says he shut himself in to receive prophecy. Ibn Ezra says he held himself back in fasting and worship. Malbim says he was ill and could not go out.

sources.quote: ידמה שהיה נסגר בחדרו ונמנע מלצאת חוץ כמנהג המתבודד להגיע אליו הנבואה
sources.says: Ralbag says he seems to have shut himself in his room, as a hermit does to receive prophecy.

sources.quote: לפני הבורא לעבדו, כעוצר עצמו מהנאה והעצור בתענית
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says he was held back before God to serve Him, holding back from pleasure, as one does in a fast.

sources.quote: כי היה עצור וחולה ולא יכול לקרא אותו אליו
sources.says: Malbim says Shemaiah was shut in and ill, so Nehemiah went to him.

6:14.headline: Noadiah: a woman prophet, or a nickname from "let us meet"?
6:14.body: Ibn Ezra reports that some took Noadiah to be Shemaiah, nicknamed from his words נועד, "let us meet" in the Temple. Ibn Ezra prefers the plain reading: Noadiah was a woman who prophesied falsely. Rashi also reads her as a woman.

sources.quote: הסכמת המפרשים שהוא שמעיה בן דליה וקראו כן, בעבור שאמר נועד אל בית האלהים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports that the commentators said this is Shemaiah son of Delaiah, called so because he said "let us meet at the house of God".

sources.quote: ולאמר כי נועדיה היתה אשה, התנבאה עליו שקר הוא הקרוב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is more likely that Noadiah was a woman who prophesied falsely against him.

sources.quote: הִיא וּשְׁאָר נְבִיאֵי הַשֶּׁקֶר
sources.says: Rashi says she and the other false prophets took money from Sanballat.

6:16.headline: Did the nations feel small, or were they amazed?
6:16.body: Rashi reads ויפלו as "they fell in their own eyes": the nations felt small. Ralbag reads it as ויפלאו, "they were amazed" that so big a wall went up so fast. Ibn Ezra says it means what it says.

sources.quote: נָפְלוּ הֵם עַצְמָם בְּעֵינֵיהֶם שֶׁהָיוּ מוֹאֲסִים בְּעַצְמָם
sources.says: Rashi says they fell in their own eyes and thought little of themselves.

sources.quote: הוא כמו ויפלאו כי זה הענין היה להם פלא עצום איך נשלמה מלאכה גדולה כזאת במעט זמן
sources.says: Ralbag says it is like ויפלאו: they were amazed that such a great work was finished so fast.

sources.quote: ואין ויפלו שם כי אם כמשמעו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says some read the word as missing an alef, but in Nehemiah it means just what it says.

7:2.headline: Was Hananiah like a man of truth, or truly one?
7:2.body: The letter כ usually means 'like', but Ibn Ezra says here it means 'truly'. Metzudat David says Hananiah was seen as a man of truth.

sources.quote: כאיש אמת - הכ"ף לאמתת הדבר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the כ here marks the thing as real.

sources.quote: כי חנניה היה נראה כאיש אמת וירא את ה׳ מימים רבים
sources.says: Metzudat David says Hananiah was seen as a man of truth who had feared God for many days.

7:3.headline: "Until the sun is hot" means the gates opened around noon
7:3.body: Nehemiah says not to open the gates until the sun is hot. Rashi and Metzudat David say this means midday, and Ralbag says it was for fear of enemies.

sources.quote: עַד חֹם הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ. עַד חֲצִי הַיּוֹם
sources.says: Rashi says 'until the sun is hot' means until the middle of the day.

sources.quote: עד חום השמש. עד יתחמם השמש בתכלית החמימות והוא בחצי היום
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means until the sun is at its hottest, which is midday.

sources.quote: שערי ירושלים (בבקר) עד חום השמש מפני יראת האויבים
sources.says: Ralbag says the gates stay shut in the morning until the sun is hot, out of fear of enemies.

7:3.headline: The order switches from "they" to "you" in mid-sentence
7:3.body: The verse first says 'they shall shut the doors', then gives a direct order to hold them fast. Ibn Ezra says Hebrew sometimes speaks to people who are present as if they were away, and he gives 'let him kiss me' as another case.

sources.quote: הכתוב בלשוננו פעם ידבר עם הנמצא כאילו נעלם ממנו, כענין: ישקני מנשיקות פיהו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says Scripture sometimes speaks to someone who is present as if he were absent, as in 'let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth'.

sources.quote: ואמר להם: אתם אחוזו הדלתות בבריחים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the order to hold is addressed to them: 'you, hold the doors with the bolts'.

7:5.headline: The word for "nobles" is traced to the Aramaic for "white"
7:5.body: החרים names the nobles. Ibn Ezra says the Aramaic for 'white' is חיור, which suggests a noble look, and nobles are called חורים from it.

sources.quote: תרגום לבן חיור והוא עין מראה נכבד וממנו נקראו חורים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the Aramaic for 'white' is חיור, that it means a noble look, and that the nobles are named חורים from it.

7:43.headline: The little letter ל here means "with"
7:43.body: The ל usually means 'to' or 'of'. Metzudat David says it stands for את, and here את means 'with', so the sons of Yeshua together with the sons of Kadmiel.

sources.quote: כי הלמ״ד הוא במקום את ואת הוא כמו עם
sources.says: Metzudat David says the ל stands in place of את, and את here means 'with'.

7:64.headline: ויגאלו means "made unclean", not "redeemed"
7:64.body: The root usually means to redeem. Here Metzudat Zion reads it as dirtied and rejected, like the 'defiled bread' in Malachi, so these men were barred from the priesthood.

sources.quote: ענין טנוף ומאוס וכן לחם מגואל
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means being soiled and rejected, as in 'defiled bread' in Malachi 1.

sources.quote: ולכן נמאסו מן הכהונה
sources.says: Metzudat David says that is why they were rejected from the priesthood.

9:5.headline: God is above all blessing, and Rashi reads this two ways
9:5.body: The Levites say God's name is lifted above all blessing and praise. Rashi gives two readings: every blessing already belongs to God, or no creature can praise God as much as God deserves.

sources.quote: כִּי כָל הַבְּרָכוֹת וּתְהִלּוֹת שֶׁלּוֹ הֵם. דָּבָר אַחֵר: וּמְרוֹמַם עַל כָּל בְּרָכָה וּתְהִלָּה שֶׁאֵין בְּרִיָּה יְכוֹלָה לְבָרְכוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says either all blessings are God's own, or no creature is able to bless God enough.

sources.quote: שלא נוכל לברכו ולהללו בשום פנים שלא יהיה ה' יתברך מרומם על כל הברכות ותהלות ההם ואפילו מלאכי השרת
sources.says: Ralbag says no blessing we give, not even the angels' blessing, reaches as high as God.

9:14.headline: God made Shabbat known: through the manna, or as creation's lesson
9:14.body: Ralbag says the manna showed them which day was Shabbat, even before Sinai. Malbim says Shabbat itself taught them that God made the world.

sources.quote: ואת שבת קדשך הודעת להם קודם זה בדבר המן שנתבאר בו לכל ישראל איזה יום הוא שבת
sources.says: Ralbag says God made Shabbat known earlier, through the manna, which showed all Israel which day was Shabbat.

sources.quote: ואמר הודעת להם כי בשבת הודיע להם פנות האמונה מחידוש העולם
sources.says: Malbim says the verse says 'made known' because through Shabbat God taught them the basics of faith, that the world was created.

9:17.headline: They only talked of picking a leader to take them back
9:17.body: ויתנו ראש reads like 'they appointed a head'. Ibn Ezra says it happened only in words: they said they would choose a leader, as in Numbers 14:4.

sources.quote: ויתנו ראש - בדבור, ופירש: אמרו לתת להם ראש כענין נתנה ראש
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says this was in speech: they said they would give themselves a head, like 'let us appoint a head'.

sources.quote: אמרו לעשות לעצמם ראש לשוב למצרים לעבדם כמאז
sources.says: Metzudat David says they spoke of making themselves a leader to go back to Egypt and serve as before.

9:21.headline: Their feet did not swell like rising dough
9:21.body: בצקו comes from בצק, dough. Metzudat David says their feet did not puff up the way dough rises, as walkers' feet usually do.

sources.quote: לא נפחו להיות כבצק הזה כאשר יתחמץ ועולה למעלה וכדרך שאר הולכי רגל
sources.says: Metzudat David says their feet did not swell like dough that rises, as happens to other people who walk far.

sources.quote: ענין עיסה המחומץ
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word is about leavened dough.

9:22.headline: Who was split off to the corner: Israel or the nations?
9:22.body: לפאה means 'to a corner' or edge. Rashi says Israel was set apart in its own corner, away from other nations, while Ibn Ezra says the nations were scattered to the corners as they fled.

sources.quote: כְּמוֹ לִהְיוֹת לְצַד זָוִית אַחַת מֻחְלָקִים, בְּלִי לְהִתְעָרֵב עִם גּוֹיֵי הָאֲרָצוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says Israel was divided off to one corner, so as not to mix with the nations.

sources.quote: דבק עם העממים והטעם פזרתם לפאות וברחו מפני ישראל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word goes with the nations: God scattered them to the corners and they fled from Israel.

9:25.headline: They grew fat, or they fattened their hearts
9:25.body: Metzudat David reads וישמינו simply: they grew fat and fleshy. Ibn Ezra says the verb acts on something else: they fattened their hearts.

sources.quote: נעשו שמנים ובעלי בשר
sources.says: Metzudat David says they became fat and fleshy.

sources.quote: פועל יוצא והטעם והשמינו לבם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the verb takes an object, meaning they made their hearts fat.

9:26.headline: Why warning someone is said with the word for witness
9:26.body: העידו comes from עד, witness, but here it means the prophets warned the people. Metzudat David says this is because people who warn usually do it in front of witnesses, so it cannot be denied later.

sources.quote: התרו בם כי רוב המתרים מתרים בעדים למען לא יכחש
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means they warned them, since most people who warn do so before witnesses so it cannot be denied.

9:30.headline: What God drew out: mercy, or the years
9:30.body: ותמשך means 'you drew out'. Rashi says God drew out mercy so as not to destroy them, and Ibn Ezra says God drew out the years in case they would return.

sources.quote: מָשַׁכְתָּ עֲלֵיהֶם רַחֲמִים, שֶׁלֹּא לְהַשְׁחִיתָם
sources.says: Rashi says God drew mercy over them so as not to destroy them.

sources.quote: השנים הם המשוכות והטעם הארכת להם אולי ישובו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the years are what was drawn out: God gave them more time in case they would return.
